criterion_comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md:3 'Preserve its ... palette'; production-plar.txt:62-73 identity 'Preserve the supplied subject, proportions, palette and south frame.' Measured source palette: #25354a (180 px), #56b5bc (186 px), #f4dda2 (24 px), nothing else. The brief does not say whether a turned view may add a shade.
criterion_comparisons.authority_basis: Mixed: 'no colour outside the source palette' is the owner outcome; reading 'preserve' as 'exactly this set, nothing added' is the specialist's interpretation, flagged in choices.palette_exact_set.
criterion_comparisons.literal_delta: Literal check: every opaque pixel is one of the three colours (strictest reading).
criterion_comparisons.discriminating_alternative: An east view adding one darker teal for the side face while keeping the three colours; the check rejects it. In pixel art 'preserve its palette' ordinarily means keep the colour set, so the caller adopts the strict reading for this assignment and records it as a reading, not a quotation.
criterion_comparisons.disposition: Keep the strict check. CORRECT THE REQUEST: the discovered declaration (connection.json schema properties.palette / palette_name) accepts hex colours and states every drawn pixel is one of them while supplied pixels stay as they are. Add palette ['#25354a','#56b5bc','#f4dda2'] to provider-arguments so the requirement is met at generation rather than by post-correction. Keep deterministic palette correction as the fallback, recorded as an 'edited' member distinct from raw provider bytes.

criterion_comparisons.source_obligation: BRIEF.md:3 'Preserve its subject ... do not redesign'; production-plar.txt:74-80 'Keep this exact south-facing sprite and its subject identity when producing other directions.' The source shows two 4x6 posts at the frame's top corners (columns 7-10 and 21-24, rows 3-8), a teal panel and two 3x4 eyes.
criterion_comparisons.authority_basis: Required outcome (identity, no redesign); the feature list is the specialist's description of the measured source.
criterion_comparisons.scope: The east candidate compared with the source at native and 3x
criterion_comparisons.literal_delta: Adds 'two square antenna posts on top' to the identity reading for every facing, plus 'eyes wherever the facing shows the front'.
criterion_comparisons.discriminating_alternative: A correct east profile of a box whose two posts sit at the left and right ends of the front edge: from the side one post occludes the other, so one post (or one with the far one partly visible) is seen. Same robot, no redesign, yet the literal 'two ... posts' clause could reject it. The posts are also 4 wide by 6 tall, not square.
criterion_comparisons.disposition: CLARIFY: for east/west require 'the antenna post(s) as visible from that facing (one may hide the other in profile), same post height'; replace 'square' with 'rectangular (4x6 in the source)'. Keep the no-added-features clause.
